thread.title_full: Battlefield 6 Season 5 Update Sparks Backlash Over AI Skins

author: priyanka.patel tech editor
title: Battlefield 6 Season 5 Update Sparks Backlash Over AI Skins
text:
Battlefield 6 released its Season 5 update, introducing the Area 51 map alongside battle pass cosmetics that sparked player backlash over suspected artificial intelligence generation, including characters with multiple pistols and misspelled security patches.
The latest content drop for EA’s hit shooter brought familiar praise for its new arena alongside sharp criticism for its cosmetic design choices. While fans welcomed the inclusion of Area 51 as one of the game’s standout additions, the accompanying battle pass rewards drew immediate scrutiny across social media following the release of Season 5, Siege of Vegas, earlier this week.
Cosmetic Flaws and Five-Pistol Skins Spark Community Backlash Players quickly pointed out several jarring visual errors and redundancies within the new tier of unlockable gear. The complaints centered on specific character models featuring questionable tactical equipment arrangements, such as redundant magazine pouches and a character outfitted with an unusual number of sidearms.
Why tf does this dude have FIVE pistols on him?
Unnamed fan, via Kotaku Another user on the Battlefield 6 subreddit voiced similar frustration over the aesthetic choices approved for the paid content.
This new Season 5 battle pass skin has five identical pistols on his kit. The cringe mask is one thing but who at BF Studios approves these dumb af character designs?
Unnamed fan, via Kotaku Beyond the excessive weaponry, community members highlighted structural design flaws on other character kits, noting that magazine placements on secondary models defied functional logic and heavily resembled automated outputs.
Misspelled Patches and the Debate Over Paid AI Assets The most concrete evidence cited by players pointing toward automated generation involved a text error on an in-game uniform. An arm patch on one of the disputed operator models features a severe typographical mistake, spelling the word security incorrectly right above the correct spelling.
Photo: Kotaku Magazine design on the second guy makes absolutely zero sense lol looks like AI-generated…then there’s the guy with the five pistols, the most egregious one is the fucking misspelled security patch lol.
Unnamed fan, via Kotaku Discussion on the platform quickly turned toward the financial model of charging real currency for assets suspected of lacking human curation. Multiple threads arguing that charging players for AI-generated content is peak disrespect accumulated thousands of upvotes as player frustration mounted over the economic value of the pass.
Historical Studio Pressure and Past Content Slip-Ups While developer confirmations regarding the use of generative tools in Season 5 remain absent, this is not an entirely new hurdle for the franchise. The title previously shipped similar cosmetics shortly after launch that took months to patch out, pointing to a recurring pipeline issue at the studio.
Instagram Observers note that these technical oversights arrive during a difficult operational window for the team.
